title: Playing what you can think of, and Boyd's performers
summary: A Teagarden quote leads Handy to say he is not tough on players, and Schremp asks about Boyd's performances of his pieces.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: He's quoted as saying something not unlike you, somebody was talking about what he did, the technique that went into his work and the thought that went into his playing, and the emotions that went into his playing and as an aside he said, that's all horseshit, I just play what I can think of.
You do what you have to and you hope that you're doing it in a way that will reach what you think you're trying to reach. That's one point, and then of course the other

point is if you're reproducing something that's been written and you've got to get every note out perfectly, and if you can make people believe that you're doing that, you're accomplishing something, even if you're not actually producing what they think you're producing.
From the other side, were you or are you tough on players who don't reproduce exactly what you've asked them to?

I'm not a tough guy, in any sense. I'm tough on nobody. If people don't reproduce what I ask them to, and they're not capable of doing it, well I discover that and I make a decision; do I want them anyway, should I adjust to them or am I insistent on what I want? If I am insistent in having what I want, I would have to change the man. But otherwise--

When you were doing (Sally)" the thing for Boyd, "Dalvatore" and "k.y F" and all that material which was astonishing to those people I'm sure, and puzzling, were you satisfied with what they finally did in performance?
Yeah; right. You better switch that off for a moment.
